newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin says Russia to pay tsarist debts.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin says Russia to pay tsarist debts.

text.p: Russia will honour debts run up by the tsarist government and later reneged on by Soviet communists, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Monday, adding that some details still had to be worked out.
He was asked as he boarded a flight to Paris if he intended to finalise an agreement to repay the debts during his visit to France, where many of the heirs to the tsar's creditors live.

"We will. I think today we will resolve this question. We will, because we are Russia. We will pay all our debts," Chernomyrdin told reporters. Details such as the repayment period had still to be settled, he added.
The successors of the original French buyers are claiming back some 140 to 160 billion francs ($27.35-$31.26 billion), taking account of unpaid interest since the revolution.
It was not clear how much of that Moscow is prepared to pay.
Moscow argues that any liability for tsarist-era debt must be offset against the seizure of Russian assets in the West after 1917 which were used to help fight the communists.
The Paris bourse suspended trading in tsarist-era Russian debt on Monday on the eve of talks with Chernomyrdin on compensation for French bond holders, officials said.

Russia returned to the international capital markets last Thursday with a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond, but it was not placed in France because of outstanding compensation claims by holders of debt issued before the revolution.
Chernomyrdin was due in Paris on Monday night for two days of talks on closer economic relations.
French officials said the debt negotiation was complex and they doubted a deal could be struck during Chernomyrdin's visit.

Russia defaulted on its loans, used to finance projects such as the Transsiberian railroad, after the Communists seized power. French investors were heavy buyers of the bonds, issued between 1822 and 1913, and thousands of small savers were left holding virtually worthless certificates.

On October 29, Russian news agency Itar-Tass quoted Finance Minister Alexander Livshits as saying that French and Russian negotiators were close to agreement on a "symbolic" gesture. ($1=5.118 French Franc)
